reviews.specification:
Implement versioned short-material-refuge with inspect, test-cover, test-joint, assess, assemble, proof-test, measure-exposure, repair, dismantle, resume and cancel modes. Public schema: {mode:enum,project:string,target:string,components:[{item:string,quantityTenths:positiveInteger,role:enum(pole,cover,binding,load)}],x:number,y:number,angle:number,width:number,length:number,height:number}; additionalProperties:false. Unused references are empty and unused dimensions zero. References use exact persistent IDs or one item:/object: prefix, never resource aliases; validate ownership, reach <=0.65, reservations and shared geometry before charging. Dependencies: personal shelter-material-metrology mastery for dimensional/load evidence; implement hand-twisted grass binding and interlaced grass-cover mechanics here without requiring an absolute-hardness tool. Public implementation supplies neither materials nor personal mastery.
Smallest design: two triangular end frames, each using two intact short poles, supporting one intact ridge; an interlaced cover slopes over the ridge. No splicing or unsupported pole extension. Dimensions are explicit and may be smaller than a resting actor; never enlarge the resulting coverage. Use measured lower lengths, actual joints, overlap and deformation to solve component endpoints. Assess returns a feasible bounded plan, an unresolved dependency, or a physical failure with reasons; it allocates nothing and cannot certify unknown inputs. Prototype limits: ridge length <= its measured lower usable length; each leg must reach its solved endpoint with 0.05 joint allowance. Ground contact and spread stability must be checked against actual slope, friction and loading. No anchoring to unverified natural objects.
Add versioned physical state for grass bundles, bindings and cover: actual input mass, origin lineage, twist/interlace progress, tensile capacity, slipping, aperture geometry, moisture and wear. Existing grass receives no retroactive certification. Declare conservative simulation laws, not measured actor knowledge: completed cover uses at least 0.5 grass mass per covered geometric area; each joint requires at least 0.02 binding mass. Grass binding strength is 50 N per unit dry binding mass, multiplied by 0.5 when saturated and by remaining integrity; slipping begins above half its breaking force. Cover geometry retains actual gaps and overlap. Paid tests compare actual force and deformation against these laws, with uncertainty; resource names alone never authorize assembly. Moisture interpolates continuously, and deterioration reduces integrity by 0.001 per elapsed round dry or 0.004 saturated. Record these model additions separately from observations.
Inspect/assess: one round, 0.2 energy. Cover and joint trials: two rounds, 0.5 energy each, explicit grass allocation of at least 0.1 unit plus actual measured pole/weight fixtures; create a retained test coupon, apply gravity from allocated masses, and record openings, sag, slipping or breakage. Test material is not pristine construction stock afterward. Assemble: four stages at 0.75 energy each—make bindings, form end frames, attach ridge, interlace cover. Reject insufficient quantities before escrow; physically consumed or incorporated fractions stay in outputs with provenance. Proof-test: two rounds at 0.5 energy, with explicit real loads at named structural points; compute self-weight, wet-cover weight, joint forces, buckling, spread and deflection using existing specimen mechanics. A pass applies only to the tested structure and bounded loading/moisture envelope, not an entire material batch. Measure-exposure: one round, 0.2 energy, records actual occupied-point solar, rain and wind exposure against an unobstructed same-weather reference; night or absent rain cannot establish their respective attenuation. Repair uses explicit replacement inputs and repeats affected proof stages. Dismantle takes two rounds at 0.5 energy and returns only surviving recoverable components.
Persist exact operation IDs, component identities, location-bound owner-retained escrow, completed stages, paid energy, remaining work, test conditions, damage and evidence. Insufficient energy pauses without progress or charges. Movement or another action pauses attended work; resume validates the same surviving components and pays only remaining stages. Cancel or death stops all owned multi-round controllers and releases surviving unincorporated escrow once at its actual location; incorporated material remains in the partial structure. No cloning, deletion, refunds or repeated completed-stage charging. Passive weathering continues after cancellation or death.
Use actual pole capsules, cloth triangles, apertures and joint locations in shared collision, interaction, roof-ray and weather calculations. Only intercepted rays reduce exposure, bounded by existing shelter attenuation limits; gaps, orientation and collapsed parts reduce coverage. Wind loading and rain accumulation can cause slipping or collapse. Neither the plan nor a tiny canopy guarantees whole-body shelter, cooling, safety or a rest bonus. Render paid intermediate work and final geometry, including failures, gaps, sag and wetting. Declare short-refuge-inspected, short-refuge-trial, short-refuge-assessed, short-refuge-progress, short-refuge-completed, short-refuge-exposure and short-refuge-stopped events with operation identity, actual inputs/outputs, remaining work, geometry revision, damage and measured uncertainty for replay and subscriptions.
Migration is additive: retain old projects, specimen bounds, uncertainties, shelter contracts and evidence applicability; do not convert old tests into new joint or cover certificates. request.name: Short-material refuge feasibility
request.function: Assess whether a small useful shade refuge can be constructed from actual short branches and locally available covering or binding materials, with an explicit feasible design only if physical evidence supports it.
request.conditions: My measured branch item-142-moss-834 has usable length bounds 0.75–0.85, below the existing shelter's 1.8 ridge and 1.2 rafter requirements. Another branch passed only its exact 1.2 supported-span test. Available dry grass is observed nearby, but its roofing and binding suitability is unknown. Bark inspection of canopy-69 found no represented separable layer. Absolute stone hardness remains unresolved.
request.inputs: Actual owned or gathered materials only; required quantities, material tests, design geometry and assembly method remain to be established.
request.costs: Unknown; require finite paid testing and construction, conserved materials, explicit failure risks and no supplied tools or resources.
request.effects: Provide a reusable feasibility assessment or physically supported alternative shelter workflow using short materials, with actual exposure reduction verified after construction. Preserve existing uncertainty, structural limits and survival constraints; do not grant shelter, material certification or wellbeing from the request itself.

projects.goal: Establish material feasibility before committing construction materials.

projects.question: Can I obtain suitable materials for a calibrated food mass assay?
evidence: Ticks 80–81: inspected actual stone and branch contact geometry.

projects.goal: Establish usable material evidence without treating relative resistance as absolute certification.

projects.pauseReason: Existing methods cannot establish the absolute prerequisite for assay fabrication.
projects.benefit: Established relative material resistance without injury or unsupported tool certification.
